title: Omega-3 and DHA in Pregnancy: Food Sources and Supplement Cautions
excerpt: The role of DHA, low-mercury fish options, and when to ask a clinician about supplements.
content:
## Introduction to Omega-3 and DHA
Omega-3 and DHA are essential nutrients for the health of both mother and baby during pregnancy. DHA (Docosahexaenoic acid) plays a crucial role in the development of the fetal brain and vision.

## Food Sources of Omega-3 and DHA
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), food sources rich in omega-3 and DHA include fatty fish such as salmon, tuna, and mackerel. However, it's essential to be aware of the mercury levels in fish, as mercury can harm fetal development. Fish with low mercury levels like salmon, sardines, and trout are good options.

## Food Safety Considerations
During pregnancy, it's crucial to consider food safety to avoid bacterial and foodborne illnesses. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pregnant women should avoid eating raw fish, sashimi, and sushi, as they can contain bacteria and parasites that can harm the fetus. Additionally, it's essential to cook food thoroughly and avoid eating processed or high-risk foods.

## Omega-3 and DHA Supplements
Omega-3 and DHA supplements can be an option for pregnant women who cannot get enough nutrients from food. However, it's essential to consult a healthcare provider before taking supplements, as they can interact with other medications or have side effects. According to the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), it's essential to choose high-quality supplements from reputable manufacturers.

## Practical Tips
To get enough omega-3 and DHA from food, try the following recipes:
- Grilled salmon with roasted vegetables
- Tuna salad with whole wheat bread
- Sardine salad with mixed greens and cherry tomatoes
You can also check out our [pregnancy meal planner](/blog/pregnancy-meal-planner) for more recipe ideas rich in omega-3 and DHA.

## When to Consult a Healthcare Provider
If you have any questions or concerns about omega-3 and DHA, consult a healthcare provider. Especially if you're pregnant and planning to take supplements, consult a healthcare provider before taking them.
